{
  "rules": [
    "If sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward bias.",
    "If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates drop; increase downward bias or add early correction.",
    "After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots and fails to correct; apply lagged mean reversion or dampen momentum.",
    "When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish (or vice versa) within 3–5 days, model often misjudges the pivot; adjust forecast to align with sentiment reversal timing.",
    "Model consistently underestimates true price volatility in bearish sentiment periods; increase forecast variance or add downward drift component.",
    "In low sentiment (0.00–0.33) with sustained price decline, model often fails to predict bottoming; add early warning signal or trigger downward correction rule.",
    "If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending, model often fails to capture mean reversion; apply smoothing or momentum decay filter.",
    "Forecast horizon 30d is prone to overfitting to recent sentiment; reduce forecast sensitivity to sentiment if sentiment is volatile or inconsistent."
  ]
}
